questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders together.
Turn your shoulders, but not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to move.
Move into a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When stopping, a motorcycle needs:

options.text: About the same stopping distance as a car.
More stopping distance than a car.
Less stopping distance than a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: About the same stopping distance as a car.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need about the same distance to stop as cars do.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.
Stay closer to the vehicle ahead.
Stay farther from the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther from the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Slow down and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: If parked vehicles are on your right and no cars are coming toward you, ride in:

options.text: The left part of your lane.
The right part of your lane.
The center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left part of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane to avoid car doors opening and people stepping out between vehicles. If traffic is coming toward you, stay in the center of your lane for more space around you.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, ride in:

options.text: The left part of the lane.
The center of the lane.
The right part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center of the lane.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding on either side can increase the risk of a collision or cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: While riding, you should wear:

options.text: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
A helmet to protect your hearing.
A baseball cap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a full-face helmet. Use hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: When riding with a group in a staggered formation:

options.text: Use it all the time.
Don't use it when entering or leaving a highway.
Use it when riding in curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't use it when entering or leaving a highway.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation for normal riding. Switch to single-file when turning, riding in curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Means they see you.
Doesn't guarantee they will yield to you.
Guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doesn't guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Eye contact doesn't guarantee a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still fail to see them.

questions.question: A difference between goggles and a windshield is:

options.text: Goggles protect you from wind, but a windshield doesn't.
A windshield protects you from wind, but goggles don't.
A windshield prevents your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect you from wind, but a windshield doesn't.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from the wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through the intersection carefully.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop and wait for a signal that allows you to turn.

questions.question: A front wheel wobble or shaking of the handlebars is usually caused by:

options.text: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight.
The front wheel not being fastened tightly to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight.
questions.explanation: A wobble is shaking of the front wheel and handlebars from side to side. Most wobbles happen because of improper weight loading, poor accessories, or wrong tire pressure.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black words or symbols. They tell you about dangerous road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What is the best position to ride in within a lane?

options.text: The left position
The right position
There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: There is no one best lane position and no position to always avoid. A good rider changes position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean in the direction you are turning.
Slow down while turning.
Turn using only the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction you are turning.
questions.explanation: Always lean in the direction of your turn. Slow down before you enter the turn.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center of the lane:

options.text: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
The driver will have trouble seeing you.
You should avoid this position.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Usually this is the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position helps them see you.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake immediately and then re-apply it.

questions.question: When getting ready to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: The left portion
The center portion
The right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: When preparing to pass on the left, ride in the left part of your lane. This gives you a better view ahead and helps drivers in the next lane see what you are about to do.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: The outside of the curve
The inside of the curve
Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Each curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: How should you stop a motorcycle in a non-emergency situation?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use both the front and rear brakes together. Also downshift as you brake.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle in hot weather, should you wear a protective jacket?

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool off.
Remove the jacket to stay cool in the sun.
Keep the jacket on for protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on for protection.
questions.explanation: A good riding jacket protects you in a crash, even in hot weather. Jackets also help prevent dehydration. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you from overheating.

questions.question: Is it a good idea to use all three lane positions while riding?

options.text: No, because you won't get used to any part of the lane.
No, because it confuses other drivers.
Yes, if you are adjusting to changing road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if you are adjusting to changing road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: How high can motorcycle handlebars be positioned?

options.text: At or higher than the rider's shoulders
At or higher than the rider's waist
At or lower than the rider's shoulders

questions.correctAnswerText: At or higher than the rider's shoulders
questions.explanation: It is illegal to ride a motorcycle if the handlebars are at or above shoulder height.

questions.question: Which surface is least likely to cause poor traction for a motorcycle?

options.text: Dry pavement
A dirt or gravel road
A shiny surface

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates or covers in the road all reduce traction. Dry pavement provides the best grip for motorcycle tires.
